Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with new-onset left-sided posterior headache since yesterday, gradual build-up to throbbing pain rated 8/10, no neurologic or systemic red flags.
- Advised trial of a stronger NSAID (instead of ibuprofen) with food; may add acetaminophen. Rest and hydration. Safety-netting and follow-up if not improving within 1–2 days or if red flags develop.

- Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, tingling, numbness, weakness, blurred vision, visual phenomena, photophobia (no problems looking at light), fever, chills, sweats, rash, neck stiffness.
- Medications tried: Ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday with no relief.

- Social/impact: Difficulty performing work/normal activities; no missed work.

- Plan discussed: Trial stronger NSAID (instead of ibuprofen) with food; may take acetaminophen concurrently; rest and maintain hydration; seek care if worsening, new symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), or recurrent episodes; call back if not improving within 1–2 days after starting medication.
